title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is building an axiomatic combinatorial-topological framework. A 'multiplicité' or 'magicien' M is a set of 'structures' (cells or simplices, possibly coming from several subdivisions at once). It carries several relations:
- ⊴ / ≪ : 'is a face of';
- ≪̊ : a refined face relation, probably 'open' or codimension-type incidence;
- || : 'meets';
- |∘| : an irreflexive 'strict/open incidence';
- ≍ : a comparability or dimension-type relation.
A 'figure' F, or a set 𝔏 of structures, lives inside M.

Previous page, Ex. 2: in a triangle (a,b,c) subdivided by a point d on the side bc, take 𝔏 = {d}. Then:
- 𝔏 |∘| X for X = (a,b,d) and for X' = (b,d);
- 𝔏 || Y for Y = (a,b,c);
- but not 𝔏 |∘| Y' for Y' = (b,c), although d lies on (b,c).
So the naive 'contractible support' of 𝔏 is not open, and a residual object along a figure cannot be defined by simply taking all structures meeting F.

This page draws the moral: 'attention à la définition des magiciens résiduels d'une figure F (ici {d}, figure ponctuelle!)'. One must restrict to X with X |∘| 𝔏 and X ≭ 𝔏. He notes that in dimension 1, exceptionally, X |∘| 𝔏 already implies X ≭ 𝔏.

He proposes the 'magicien résiduel le long de 𝔏':
M' = { X ∈ M | X |∘| 𝔏, X ≭ 𝔏 }.
He then proves that M' is a sub-magicien (sub-multiplicity). Concretely, M' must satisfy a parallelogram closure condition: given X ≪̊ Y and X' ≪̊ Y' with X' ⊴ X and Y' ⊴ Y, if X, Y, X' ∈ M' then Y' ∈ M'.

Proof:
1. Y ≭ 𝔏 and Y' ⊴ Y give Y' ≭ 𝔏 (heredity of ≭ under faces).
2. So it remains to see Y' |∘| 𝔏, which reduces to Y' ∉ 𝔏.
3. If Y' ∈ 𝔏, then X' |∘| 𝔏 gives X' |∘| Y'. Combined with X' ≪̊ Y', this yields X' |∘| X', contradicting irreflexivity.

Modern reading: for a simplicial or regular-cell complex, the set of cells having a given cell or subcomplex as a proper face is the open star minus the cell itself. As a poset this is isomorphic to the link. So the 'residual magician along 𝔏' is an axiomatic version of the link / transverse structure along a stratum, defined so as to be stable under the change-of-subdivision ('multi-structure') relations.
errors: The argument is correct given the implicit axioms: heredity of ≭ under ⊴, the reduction of |∘| 𝔏 to non-membership, and irreflexivity of |∘|. These axioms are not stated on this page, so the proof is only as complete as the earlier definitions.
The interpretation of the symbols |∘|, ||, ≍, ≪̊ is inferred from the example on the previous page and remains uncertain.

ideas.what: Counterexample: for a point figure d on an edge of a subdivided triangle, the coarse edge (b,c) contains d geometrically but is not 'strictly incident' to d. Hence 'support/cosupport' of a figure is not open and residual structures must be defined carefully.
ideas.modern_name: Failure of star/support to be compatible with coarsening of subdivisions; links in PL topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard PL topology (Alexander, Newman, Whitehead; Rourke–Sanderson)

ideas.what: Definition of the residual magician along a figure 𝔏, M' = {X | X |∘| 𝔏, X ≭ 𝔏}, and proof that it is closed under the parallelogram (face/refined-face) condition.
ideas.modern_name: Link of a simplex/stratum (upper link, open star minus the cell), transverse structure along a stratum
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical simplicial/PL topology; stratified-space links (Thom, Mather, Goresky–MacPherson)
ideas.where_published: Unpublished 1986 notes; the tame-topology program is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) §5–6, but not this formalism

ideas.what: Remark that dimension 1 is exceptional: strict incidence already forces non-comparability.
ideas.modern_name: Low-dimensional degeneracy of incidence relations in cell posets

missed.claim: The 'magiciens/multiplicités' formalism is an unpublished attempt at an axiomatic combinatorial (tame/PL-like) topology that allows several subdivisions simultaneously ('multi-structures'). It includes residual (link) constructions along figures and, on the next page, compactness axioms. It was never developed or published. This page contributes the link construction and its subtlety under refinement.
missed.quote: attention à la définition des magiciens résiduels d'une figure (ici {d}, figure ponctuelle!)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is relevant to combinatorial/poset models of stratified spaces and to 'tame topology' in the sense of Esquisse. It also bears on handling subdivision invariance of links axiomatically. A historian might connect it to later o-minimal and exit-path/poset approaches, but the content here is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries a correct but routine lemma: the link/residual sub-structure is closed under the refinement condition, plus a small cautionary counterexample. It is interesting only as part of Grothendieck's unpublished 1986 axiomatic combinatorial topology; the mathematics itself is standard.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'régions[?] résiduelles' is more likely 'magiciens résiduels' (the handwriting reads 'm.giciens r.siduels').
Left margin: likely 'magicien résiduel le long de 𝔏', not 'multiplicité résiduelle'.
'prendre[?] 𝒜≥3[?] dans ≪[?] dans une sous-multiplicité' is unreliable; the sense is roughly 'pour [obtenir] une sous-magicien, se borner aux X telles que X ≭ F'.
The relation in the commutative square and in the last line is ≪̊ (circled ≪), as on the previous page, rather than ≤̊; the vertical arrows are ⊴ (written ▽/).
